data.narrative:
Valar Atomics, a Series B nuclear energy company, currently carries a $6.0B post-money valuation after raising $1.0B to date. The broader nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies, with notable private-stage peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Aalo Atomics.

Valuation triangulation relied on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median comparison proved inapplicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints at the same stage and valuation tier. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the current $6.0B post-money base, yielding an implied valuation of $11.4B. This represents the median point in a derived range anchored at $9.7B (low) and $13.1B (high).

The analysis supports a median valuation of $11.4B, with reasonable bounds spanning $9.7B to $13.1B. Given the single-method dependency, key uncertainties center on whether the 1.9x stage multiplier appropriately reflects Valar Atomics' specific path to Series C or beyond, and the extent to which broader nuclear sector momentum (represented by the 11-company comp set) may compress or expand typical multiplier assumptions. Direct peer-stage comparables remain a critical data gap for validation.
